answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted reputation that accrues slowly through verified work: each identity posts a bond and builds a history of completed tasks before transacting at full volume. Like a saffron harvest, trust is gathered grain by grain, not bought in bulk. A new account starts on a small knoll of permissions and only climbs higher as peers attest to real performance, so a flood of fake identities is a river in drought — many channels, little water — and mass fakery stays expensive and slow.
